In English, the sentence structure usually follows the same sequence: subject + verb + object. The subject comes first and the object comes last. However, if you don't want to pay special attention to the subject, you can change the word order. One way of doing this is by using the passive voice to change the focus in a sentence.

The passive voice allows you talk about an event or action from the point of view of the thing or person affected. Sometimes you can write a sentence without even mentioning the agent (who or what was responsible for the action).
This is how the passive is formed:  thing receiving action + be + past participle + (by) + (thing doing action)
In informal spoken English, get is sometimes used instead of be to form the passive.
The meeting was scheduled without prior notice.
I wasn't pressured to make this decision.
This decision was predicted and based on the model that we followed.
All I can say is that you are very much appreciated here.
You use the Present Perfect tense to talk about a past action or an action that began in the past that is connected to the present in some way.

You can use the Present Perfect tense to talk about experience.

This is how you form the Present Perfect: subject + have + past participle
When you use the Present Perfect tense, you think about the past and present together. There is some connection between what happened in the past and now.
The Present Perfect is also used to emphasize the duration of a recent event.
We've been under a lot of stress lately.
I want to say that you've done a superb job.
This has been a time for me to reconsider my goals in life.
I've run out of words.

images.text:
Janet: Thanks for coming everyone. This meeting was scheduled last minute and an important message needs to be communicated. All I can say is I hope that a good time was had by all.
Ferdinand: Thanks, Janet.
Miranda: What's going on? What are you trying to say, Janet?
Janet: I'm going to keep this brief. We've been under a lot of pressure lately. All of us. And you have all done an amazing job. I can see that we have been strengthened as a team and have learned many skills. That was predicted in Miranda's model of crisis management. I too have gained insight into my own priorities and personal objectives.

Miranda: Janet, perhaps we should have a private discussion ...
Janet: It's alright, Miranda. This has been a time to reconsider our goals, reposition ourselves, develop our own true philosophies and find ways to practice them. Whether it has been learning how to act responsibly as a corporation, or remembering that there is more to successful business than making a profit, we have grown. In the light of recent events, I have decided that what I really want to do at this stage in life is charity work. I would like to build on my father's legacy and the work he supported in Tindasia.

Ferdinand: Wow! That sounds great, Janet!
Rocco: Congratulations!
Miranda: I hope you weren't pressured ...
Janet: Oh Miranda, this decision is entirely my own. I am honored to have worked with such an amazing team. You are all so much appreciated - I've run out of words.
